scope: Five supplementary 2026 or adjoining papers. This is a primary-source catalogue, not an exhaustive review or experimental replication.
user_protocol: Observed fixed empty shell, openings and complete furniture text inventory; sizes and poses unknown; output layout goes to the same RoomGenBench realization.

papers.name: Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation
papers.publication: TPAMI 2026 per arXiv comment and related DOI 10.1109/TPAMI.2026.3711762.
primary_evidence: The paper links the author project; its Code link points to haochengCop/Agentic-Designer.
Targeted reading: III-A, III-D, IV-C, IV-D, V-C and VI.
papers.input: Parametric walls, doors and windows as 2D architectural quadrilaterals. Generates furniture category, location, bounding box and orientation until End; exact supplied instance IDs are not established.
papers.method: Three independently role-finetuned Qwen2.5-Coder-7B models act as Generator, Evaluator and Refiner. Each proposal receives learned violation diagnosis and bounded refinement before commitment. Learned diagnosis is not a deterministic safety certificate.

evaluation.dataset: InStruct: 18,853 samples, comprising 10,795 living rooms and 8,058 bedrooms. Cross-dataset evaluation uses 300 living rooms and 300 bedrooms from adapted 3D-FRONT.
evaluation.metrics: ANF: mean furniture count. OR: total furniture area / room area. SVR: fraction of scenes with any boundary violation. BVC: mean violating objects per scene. CS: mean pairwise IoU multiplied by 10,000. Human CR/LR/PR assess circulation, placement and proportion on a 1–5 scale.
evaluation.human: 31 participants evaluate anonymized 2D layouts for 30 test rooms.

limitations: Author: concave boundaries and deep exterior recesses can create topological ambiguity.
2D footprint metrics do not establish mesh support, stability or door-seeded reachability.
ANF and OR do not establish exact inventory; mean pairwise IoU depends on object count.
papers.relation_to_user_task: Close architectural conditioning and dimension/pose prediction. Needs exact required IDs, 3D heights/support and the same RoomGenBench realization; architectural information must be equally available to baselines.

code.status: The official linked repository is accessible but contains presentation assets rather than implementation.
code.evidence: The complete 45-entry tree contains README, index.html, framework.png and 40 SVG examples, plus directories. No Python, model or evaluator files.
code.metric_source_status: No metric implementation in this pinned presentation tree. This is not a claim about every possible public resource.

papers.not_claimed: No independent score, timing or model reproduction. A future release promise is not treated as current availability.

papers.name: INTERIORAGENT: LLM Agent for Interior Design-Aware 3D Layout Generation
papers.arxiv_status: No exact arXiv identifier was located or verified; none is invented.
papers.publication: 3DV 2026, confirmed by primary coauthor publication pages.
papers.input: Natural-language interior design brief. Current official software retrieves and registers actual assets and builds hierarchical groups. Default room and inventory creation differs from an immutable observed shell and furniture list.
papers.method: Paper: IDSDL design-aware scene language, synthesis/optimization tools and ergonomic constraint refinement. Current repository: asset retrieval, relative/around/grid/room groups, nested builds, geometric and VLM constraints, program authoring and render/critic loops. Current software may extend the published paper.

evaluation.verified: Primary abstract reports a user study. Exact participant/sample denominators and automatic metric definitions were not independently recovered in this sub-audit because full PDF access was limited.
evaluation.current_pipeline_judge: Current README describes an internal 0–10 design judge. This is not automatically the published user study or an external benchmark.

limitations: Default creation can alter inventory and shell; constrain these for the user task.
Current pipeline needs actual assets, Blender and API-backed planning/critics; not inherently lightweight.
Published study details and exact paper-era implementation remain unverified.
papers.relation_to_user_task: Useful reference for group/anchor DSL and functional tools. Enforce canonical IDs, fixed shell/openings, shared asset information and bounded scales. Grouping, retrieval and feedback alone are established ingredients.

code.official_evidence: Repository description matches the paper title; README identifies Kunal Gupta research and links InteriorAgent documentation. Coauthor pages confirm authorship and title.
code.metric_source_status: Complete 622-entry tree and README inspected. No dedicated published benchmark suite identified. Code bodies and metric implementations were not fully audited; tests.py is a feature gallery.
commands_readme: python main.py "a cozy ramen bar with counter seating" --out results/ramen_bar
python tests.py all (feature tests; APIs and assets required)

papers.name: Co-Layout: LLM-driven Co-optimization for Interior Layout
papers.input: Text design brief. The LLM extracts room, furniture and constraint lists. It jointly designs room partitions/corridors and furniture placement. Furniture width/length are LLM-determined constants; orientation has four axis-aligned choices.
papers.method: Unified 2D grid integer program for room/corridor/furniture occupancy, exclusivity, connectivity, access and preferences, with coarse-to-fine solving. Paper uses Gurobi 12; current README recommends 13 and has revised runtime budgets.

evaluation.quantitative: Five examples; OOR overlap area percentage, OOB boundary violation rate, Q-Align IQA/IAA and CLIP text/render similarity. Holodeck and AnyHome outputs are rendered uniformly.
evaluation.human: 71 participants, 64 valid responses; 1–5 semantic, layout and path ratings plus ranking MRR.
evaluation.ablation: Coarse-to-fine timing across grid resolutions, five repeats for a fixed prompt.

limitations: Floor-based furniture only; wall and tabletop objects are future work.
LLM constraints may conflict; finite grid and four orientations restrict the layout domain.
Five quantitative examples do not establish broad ranking generalization or 3D support validity.
papers.relation_to_user_task: Strong adjacent packing/constraint reference. Disable architecture redesign for an observed shell. Its dimensions come from the LLM rather than necessarily GT; use a common non-GT size provider in a controlled comparison.

code.status: Official generation and optimization source is available.
code.official_evidence: Author homepage, project and README identify the official AAAI repository.
code.metric_source_status: Complete 51-entry tree and README inspected. No paper Q-Align/CLIP/OOR/OOB benchmark suite identified. Core optimization and rendering exist; metric code bodies were not audited.
commands_readme: python run_e2e.py (required arguments documented in README)

papers.name: OpenAsset: A Pipeline for Open-World Asset Integration into Indoor Scene Synthesis
papers.input: Text concept plus user reference photo or target region; not text-only unknown-asset generation.
papers.method: SAM 3 segmentation, SAM 3D single-image reconstruction, orientation/scale/coordinate canonicalization, then ReSpace-compatible SSR placement/editing. Uses released component checkpoints; GPT-4o captions are constructed offline.

evaluation.components: Mask mIoU, Dice and boundary F-score; reconstruction metrics; canonical orientation and relative height errors on independently annotated subsets.
evaluation.scenes: FID, CLIP-FID, KID and 5 cm voxel OOB/mesh-boundary/VBL. Closed set: 500 test scenes per split; open set: 1,000 text/image pairs.
evaluation.success: All evaluated objects grounded, in bounds and noncolliding. Angular/scale errors use reliably annotated subsets, not all open-set samples.

limitations: Depends on segmentation and single-view reconstruction; occlusion and complex geometry remain difficult.
Metric-specific GT subsets differ and their denominators need disclosure.
The grounded-on-floor criterion does not cover the full wall/ceiling/tabletop support task.
papers.relation_to_user_task: An adjacent asset-realization extension when photos are supplied. Not a direct text-inventory layout baseline; do not give only this competitor image information.

code.status: Paper-linked repository exists, but code is still marked coming soon.

code.evidence: Complete pinned tree has only a 109-byte README: paper title and code coming soon.
code.metric_source_status: No implementation or metrics in the pinned tree; paper formulas are not verified code.

papers.name: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
papers.publication: Preprint submitted 9 October 2026; no accepted venue assigned here.
papers.input: Controlled industrial requirements with fixed geometry and an 11-instance inventory, workspace, parent/attachment relations and aisle/clearance parameters. Generates a 25-operation scene program.
papers.method: Qwen3-VL-8B LoRA SFT, greedy program generation, Python state execution/save/reload and deterministic verification, followed by local projection and conflict-graph joint beam repair that preserves attachments.

evaluation.population: 2,754 candidate conditions; 1,749 constructible cases split into 1,399 train, 175 interpolation test and 175 compositional test. Unsuccessful construction does not prove mathematical infeasibility.
evaluation.geometry: 94 atoms: 11 boundary, 36 collision, 36 equipment-clearance and 11 aisle checks. GVB averages failed atoms; complete feasibility requires structural and geometric validity.
evaluation.visual: 20 fixed dual-view cards per method; OU/SO machine scores on 0–5 scale and three human raters.

limitations: Controlled fixed schema/inventory and Python state semantics; not general real-mesh or live Unity physics validation.
Constructibility filtering selects known-feasible references; it does not evaluate arbitrary infeasible inventories.
Industrial scores belong in an adjacent-work table, not the same room-layout leaderboard.
papers.relation_to_user_task: Relevant prior art for complete verification and coupled repair, but known fixed asset geometry and executable programs differ from unknown-size text inventory to RoomGenBench.

code.status: No official repository established from paper links and targeted title/arXiv searches.
code.search_boundary: This means no official link was located in this audit, not proof code cannot exist elsewhere.
code.metric_source_status: Appendix G definitions read; no metric implementation verified or executed.

synthesis.closest_protocol: Agentic Designer models architectural elements and predicts dimensions, but generates free inventory in 2D. Co-Layout infers dimensions from text but redesigns rooms on a grid. InteriorAgent requires substantial adaptation. OpenAsset and VIGOR are adjacent photo-asset and industrial tasks.
synthesis.paper_code_distinction: Each row separates paper definitions, current source availability and unverified evaluation claims. Repository existence does not establish reproduction.
novelty_implications: Stepwise agent verification before commitment already appears in Agentic Designer.
Group/anchor DSL, retrieval knowledge and render feedback already appear in InteriorAgent.
Text-driven connectivity/access co-optimization already appears in Co-Layout.
Photo-asset canonicalization/integration already appears in OpenAsset.
Complete verification and conflict-graph repair already appear in VIGOR, an industrial neighbor.
synthesis.what_remains_for_user: Use the same input, inventory, asset information and budget; retain the winning GPT one-shot baseline and independently check final RoomGenBench realizations. No ingredient alone establishes novelty.
